result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B gives a clear four-level type scale with a separate size for the restaurant name. It spells out the spacing difference between items and sections and lists the setup steps tersely. A gives good advice on tab leaders, two-decimal prices and letterspaced capitals, but it groups the restaurant name with the section headings without its own size. It also adds a pointless check on the service-charge figure and printing advice nobody asked for. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Answer A gives a complete size table covering all four levels, including the restaurant name, and spaces sections more widely than items (18 pt before each heading versus 4–6 pt between dishes). Its price treatment uses tab stops with dot leaders and two decimals. Answer B covers price alignment, letterspacing and footer size just as well, but it gives no size for the restaurant name, and its odd service-charge check and printing tangents add little.
